title: Throughput shim pilot sync
summary: Weekly POC sync to review throughput numbers from last 48h, validate continuous-batching changes, set concurrency targets, and agree on next benchmarking runs. We resolved a KV cache warming bug, agreed to a short stress run on Friday, and decided to test burst fallback to a quantized variant. Action items assigned for runbook updates and telemetry alerts.
topics: next benchmarking run and artifacts to share
action_items: Luis Ortega - add KV-cache warmup to pilot runbook + sample curl (due: 2027-11-12)
Priya Raman - schedule 2h stress window Friday 11/12 (due: 2027-11-11)
Maya Chen - share Friday benchmark template and cost/latency sheet (due: 2027-11-10)
Samir Patel - enable detailed token-level telemetry for one pod group (due: 2027-11-12)
Leah Morris - confirm product acceptance criteria for latency tail (due: 2027-11-15)
next_steps: Run 2-hour steady-state and 30-minute spike tests on Friday using the shared template
Redwood to push a small batching param change: max_batch_latency_ms from 40 -> 30 and test impact
Customer to flip on KV-cache prewarm flag during tests
Reconvene next Monday for data review and go/no-go on expansion
transcript: Meeting header: 2027-11-09 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Recording: yes
[00:00] Maya Chen: alright everyone good afternoon thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, Luis is with me from SE, how are we Priya?
[00:10] Priya Raman: hey doing good thanks, just came out of an incident earlier so slightly caffeinated but good to go
[00:15] Luis Ortega: quick FYI I pushed the micro-change to the batching runtime overnight, small param tweak, should be non-disruptive
[00:30] Samir Patel: saw the deploy, traffic looked stable on canary, but we noticed the KV cash (sic) hit rate was lower than expected during warmup
[00:45] Maya Chen: yeah that was the thing we wanted to call out — there's a prewarm ordering issue that can cause cold prefixes to miss the cache on short-lived sessions
[01:05] Leah Morris: can you explain what that looks like in our telemetry? we saw latency spikes around 10:23 UTC last night
[01:25] Luis Ortega: sure, so you'll see a tail in p95-p99 where the first chunk of requests for a new session go to disk, because the KV cache hasn't had the prefix populated — that's the warmup gap
[01:50] Priya Raman: ok so that's KV cache warmup. does Redwood have a recommended prewarm pattern?
[02:05] Maya Chen: we do — Luis will add a snippet to the runbook, basically prime prefixes during session handshake or send a tiny synthetic request right after pod start — simple and effective
[02:20] Samir Patel: that should be easy to implement. one question: how does continuous batching interact with that? if we prewarm too many prefixes does batching delay go up?

[02:40] Luis Ortega: good question. continuous batching groups by attn key and sequence length; prewarm requests are tiny so they usually get batched quickly. the bigger risk is raising max_batch_latency_ms which can increase average latency
[03:05] Leah Morris: you mentioned earlier you changed max_batch_latency_ms from 40 to 30 — any initial wins?
[03:18] Luis Ortega: initial 24-hour numbers show median latency improved 6% on synthetic traces, but throughput dropped about 3% because smaller batches formed more often — tradeoff territory
[03:40] Priya Raman: what's our target concurrency? Ops wants a cap so we don't blow the budget
[03:55] Maya Chen: for the pilot we suggested a soft concurrency target of 120 concurrent requests per GPU, with burst to 200 if backlog < 50 — that's configurable
[04:15] Samir Patel: curious on how Redwood calculates that 120 number — is it model-specific or based on observed token/s?

[04:30] Luis Ortega: it's model plus workload profile. we look at average tokens per call, kv-cache hit rate, and batch packing efficiency — we ran a quick estimate for your prompt distribution and landed near 120
[04:55] Priya Raman: okay, for budgeting we need an estimate of cost delta if we move to dedicated vs hosted — maybe later but flagging
[05:10] Maya Chen: noted — we'll send a delta sheet. for today's focus let's finish the tuning loop and set the Friday stress run
[05:25] Leah Morris: what about fallback behavior when capacity constrained? we saw an error path last week that returned 503s

[05:40] Luis Ortega: 503s happened because the autoscale threshold for the reservation group hit and requests overflowed the queue; we have two mitigation patterns: 1) fallback to a quantized model variant with lower memory and higher throughput, 2) route to a lower-tier region. we recommended config (2) for low-latency impact
[06:10] Samir Patel: fallback to quantized variant — what's the quality delta?
[06:25] Maya Chen: typically small for short prompts, sometimes visible on long-form. we'll attach eval diffs in the shared sheet so you can review tradeoffs
[06:40] Priya Raman: okay please include that. also need to make sure keys and logs are retained for audit — SOC2 plus internal policy
[06:55] Maya Chen: Redwood Private has KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs; for this pilot you are on Redwood Hosted but we can turn on extended logging and export to your SIEM for the window
[07:15] Leah Morris: that would work for now, thanks

[07:30] Luis Ortega: going back to throughput numbers — I'll surface the 48-hour run charts: overall throughput averaged 980 tokens/s per GPU group during steady-state, with spikes up to 1.5k tokens/s when burst enabled
[07:50] Samir Patel: that's promising — how did p95 and p99 behave under those spikes?
[08:05] Luis Ortega: p95 stayed within SLA at ~220ms, p99 stretched to ~720ms during a couple bursts before the queueing smoothed out; the bursts coincided with a lower-than-expected KV hit rate
[08:30] Priya Raman: 720ms p99 is borderline for our product team, Leah?
[08:38] Leah Morris: yeah we aim for p99 < 600ms for interactive features; 720ms would be a red flag for rollout
[08:50] Maya Chen: two levers: tighten batching latency (which Luis tweaked) or increase concurrency to drain queue faster — but increasing concurrency ups cost
[09:10] Samir Patel: we can tolerate slightly higher cost if p99 comes down. can you model cost delta for concurrency +20%?
[09:25] Maya Chen: yes we will run a quick cost/latency sensitivity and share a small table

[09:40] Luis Ortega: also we found a small GC pattern on one of your node images — JVM pause (customer app) was causing request bursts to pile up; once pod restarted KV warmup happened and latency spiked
[09:58] Priya Raman: that's our side, thanks for flagging. we'll schedule a restart policy tweak and bump probe thresholds
[10:15] Leah Morris: for Friday's run can Redwood expose a debug flag so we can tag requests and trace through the pipeline?
[10:30] Luis Ortega: yes, we have a request trace header you can add; we'll also drop a dashboard with token-level timing and batching stats
[10:45] Maya Chen: action items list we'll compile and attach. quick check: are we all aligned to run two steady windows (2h each) plus a burst stress?
[11:00] Priya Raman: yes that's the plan — one steady one steady and one spike, ideally in your off-peak
[11:12] Samir Patel: prefer early morning Friday to avoid affecting end users
[11:20] Maya Chen: we'll aim for 08:00 UTC Friday then. Luis will post the template and curl examples
[11:32] Leah Morris: small nit — sometimes the transcript uses the product Redwood Dedicate (sic) in our docs; let's keep naming consistent
[11:45] Luis Ortega: good call, I'll use "Redwood Dedicated" consistently and update the docs we share
[12:00] Priya Raman: what's the expected mitigation if the quantized fallback is worse than tolerable? do we have automatic rollback?
[12:18] Luis Ortega: yes, rollout policies default to automatic fallback to original model on quality regression, and we can also set up canary percentages to limit exposure
[12:35] Maya Chen: also want to call out telemetry alert thresholds — we'll propose p95 > 300ms or p99 > 600ms as signals to trigger a manual throttle or scale
[12:50] Samir Patel: sounds good. can that generate a Slack alert with a link to the dashboard?
[13:00] Luis Ortega: yes we have Slack+PagerDuty integrations; we'll include Slack with direct dashboard link in the alert payload
[13:12] Leah Morris: ok practical question: for the Friday tests do we need a config change to the queue size? last time we hit queue overflow
[13:28] Luis Ortega: you can increase queue depth from 500 -> 750 for the group, that gives more headroom for short spikes; downside is memory usage per worker increases
[13:45] Priya Raman: memory is fine, but we don't want unbounded backlog. let's stick to 750 and watch it

[14:00] Maya Chen: excellent. I'll summarize next steps here — Redwood to share runbook with KV prewarm snippet, benchmark template, and cost delta table; customer to schedule Friday window and enable telemetry flags
[14:20] Samir Patel: one last ask — can you include the small eval diffs between float and 8-bit quant variants so product can eyeball quality?
[14:35] Maya Chen: yes we'll attach eval diffs and a short notes doc on expected artifacts
[14:45] Priya Raman: perfect. thanks everyone, any final questions?
[14:55] Leah Morris: none from me, thanks
[15:00] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and post the artifacts to the shared drive. meeting adjourned
Meeting footer: shared links — runbook (https://redwood.example/runbooks/stalwart-prewarm), benchmark template (https://redwood.example/templates/throughput-template.csv), eval diffs (attached)
